title: Lauren Ash and Mae Martin join animated comedy Dirts
body_md:
Lauren Ash and Mae Martin have joined the voice cast of Dirts, an adult animated high-school comedy being developed for Shozer, the comedy platform from New Metric Media. The casting announcement, reported on November 26, 2026, also identifies Mark McKinney, Mark Little and Ryan Belleville as members of the ensemble. The series is scheduled to premiere in winter 2027, although a specific release day has not been announced.

The premise takes familiar teenage anxieties into an unusual animated setting. Gus and Brus are two deeply unpopular vegetable teenagers attending Leguma Beach High. Their school brings together privileged vine vegetables and less established root vegetables, creating a social hierarchy that gives the comedy a distinctive visual vocabulary. The unlikely friends must navigate the embarrassment, rivalry and complicated relationships associated with adolescence.

Ash, known for Superstore, voices Sproutabella, while Martin, whose credits include Wayward, plays Trevin Stems. McKinney voices Principal Corny. Little and Belleville portray Gus and Brus respectively. The supporting ensemble includes Kyle Dooley, Evany Rosen, Kayla Lorette, Rodrigo Fernandez-Stoll and Chelsea Clark, with several performers taking on multiple characters.

Dane Clark, Viveno Caldinelli and Mark Montefiore co-created the series, with Caldinelli directing. New Metric Media is producing in partnership with Little Black Stone Studios. Ariel Yang and Max Wolfond are producing for New Metric, while Tysen Potter is producing for its partner studio.

One particularly interesting production decision is that Dirts is being designed for both vertical and horizontal viewing. That approach acknowledges the growing importance of mobile viewing without abandoning conventional screen formats. The announcement does not establish whether the two versions will feature different edits or simply different framing, so that aspect remains to be seen.

Dirts is part of a wider programming slate for Shozer, which was launched by the company behind Letterkenny and Shoresy. Other announced projects include a satirical mockumentary about Canadian history and short-form comedy programming designed to introduce emerging performers. Together, these projects illustrate the company's ambition to build original comedy properties and connect directly with audiences.

For animation viewers, the combination of an ensemble school comedy and anthropomorphic vegetables offers an unusual hook. The central friendship may prove more important than the novelty of the setting, particularly if the series uses its fictional social divisions to explore recognizable teenage experiences. Whether the concept sustains a full series will depend on its writing, characterization and comic timing. Episode counts and individual running times have not been disclosed in the casting report.
excerpt: Shozer announces the voice cast and premise of its adult animated comedy.
